title: Trump Signs Executive Order Creating US Space Academy at Houston Stop
detail: President Trump signed an executive order on Friday, August 28, 2026, at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, establishing the nation's first U.S. Space Academy — a new federal institution to train personnel for the Space Force, NASA, and the civilian space industry. The order creates a Presidential Commission on the U.S. Space Academy chaired by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, and science advisor Michael Kratsios also involved; the commission has 120 days to deliver a report on governance, curriculum, and site selection, with Trump saying a location would be chosen 'very shortly.' The signing came during a Houston stop in which Trump also awarded medals to the Artemis II crew.

media.caption: Trump signs an executive order establishing the US Space Academy at NASA's Johnson Space Center

title: Judge Rejects Trump's Third Attempt to Move Hush Money Case to Federal Court
detail: US District Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein on Friday, August 28, 2026 rejected President Trump's third attempt to move his New York hush money conviction from state to federal court, where Trump's legal team hoped to invoke broader presidential immunity following a Supreme Court immunity ruling to have the conviction tossed. Hellerstein, who has now blocked the removal bid three times, wrote that 'the grounds for a second removal cited by Defendant, Donald J. Trump, are neither new nor legally sufficient' and that Trump 'failed to show good cause and diligence.' Trump was convicted in 2024 on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records tied to a $130,000 hush payment to Stephanie Clifford (Stormy Daniels).

media.caption: A federal judge rejects Trump's third bid to move his hush money case to federal court

title: Trump Announces 'Biggest Oil Deal in World History' Giving US Majority Control of Venezuela's Oil Reserves
detail: President Trump announced Friday, August 28, 2026 that the US had struck a deal with Venezuela granting a new joint venture majority US control — a 55% stake — over more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves across 17 fields, which Trump called 'THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY' and said comes 'at no cost to' American taxpayers. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth negotiated the agreement with Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodríguez under a 100-year lease; the White House projects it could draw $100 billion in private investment and generate over $209 billion in tax revenue for Caracas, and Trump claimed it would 'substantially lower' US gas prices, though no text of the agreement was released and analysts questioned how quickly the reserves could be developed. The deal follows the US military operation in Venezuela in January 2026 that captured then-president Nicolás Maduro.

media.caption: Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodríguez, who negotiated the oil deal with Secretaries Rubio and Hegseth

title: Trump Administration Appeals Boston Judge's Ruling Blocking Mail-Voting Restrictions
detail: The Trump administration filed a notice of appeal on Friday, August 28, 2026, challenging a ruling by US District Judge Indira Talwani in Boston that blocked implementation of Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting for the next two weeks. Talwani, ruling Thursday, August 27, found that states lack the time and money to redesign ballots, update systems, and train officials to comply with the order's Postal Service data-sharing requirements before the first general-election mail ballots go out September 4. The case is now before the 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals and could return quickly to the Supreme Court, which on August 24 lifted a separate injunction on the same order without ruling on its underlying legality.

media.caption: The legal fight over Trump's mail-voting executive order continues as the administration appeals a Boston judge's injunction
